entities.name: Henry II of Jerusalem
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Henry II (1271-1324) reigned as the last crowned King of Jerusalem from 1285 until the fall of Acre in 1291, and concurrently as King of Cyprus from 1285 until his death. A scion of the influential Lusignan dynasty, his reign marks the definitive end of the Crusader States' territorial presence in the Levant, a pivotal moment in the history of the Latin East. His struggle against the resurgent Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt defined the final, desperate years of Frankish rule, transforming the island of Cyprus into the primary, albeit diminished, center of Crusader power and a strategic outpost against Islamic expansion in the Eastern Mediterranean.

Ascending to the thrones of Cyprus and Jerusalem at the age of fourteen following the death of his brother John I, Henry II faced an insurmountable challenge. His early reign was dominated by the Mamluk siege of Tripoli in 1289 and, most critically, the siege and fall of Acre in 1291, which saw the complete eradication of the remaining Crusader territories on the mainland. Despite various diplomatic overtures to Western powers and attempts to forge alliances with the Mongol Ilkhanate, these efforts ultimately failed to reclaim the Holy Land. After 1291, Henry governed from Cyprus, focusing on maintaining his island kingdom and attempting to organize new crusades, albeit without success.
